title: For Alignment Conservers, inaction that permits a violation is misalignment on par with committing one
content:
A.1.5.3 sets three constraints on Alignment Conservers: they "must operate only within the clearly delineated processes and frameworks of the Immutable Documents"; they are "strictly prohibited from colluding or secretly organizing to circumvent or undermine the Spirit of the Atlas"; and "any action of an Alignment Conserver that disrupts the governance dynamic of Sky is considered misalignment, as is any inaction that allows such violations to occur."

The annotation at A.1.5.3.0.3.5 removes any doubt about weighting: inaction "refers to the failure to act when action is necessary to prevent or address breaches" and "is considered as serious as active misalignment."

This converts AC status from a set of prohibitions into a standing affirmative duty. A conserver who notices a breach and stays silent has themselves breached — which is the only coherent position for a role whose entire function is to safeguard a process. A watchman punished only for acts, never for omissions, would have a dominant strategy of watching nothing.

It also explains the collusion prohibition's specific wording. A.1.5.3.0.3.3 and .3.6 define colluding and secretly organizing in terms of *secrecy* and *malign intent* — "behind closed doors," "with the intent to undermine Universal Alignment." The prohibited thing is not coordination as such but coordination that escapes observation, because unobservable coordination defeats the mutual-monitoring the inaction duty depends on.

The cost is exposure: every AC is now liable for the whole surface they can see, and "failure to act when action is necessary" is judged after the fact by someone who knows the outcome.
description: A.1.5.3 makes any AC action that disrupts the governance dynamic misaligned, 'as is any inaction that allows such violations to occur' — converting AC status into a standing duty to intervene.
